text.insert: Kernel trace linkage joins accepted game events to runtime spans through protected metadata and a persisted game-cycle cursor. It preserves the kernel's existing schema and makes optional telemetry distinguishable from failed durable linkage.

A workflow trace submission requires nonblank game, game-event, and correlation identities plus an explicit caused-by event identity or null. The durable game event is loaded by game and event identity. Its correlation and resolved same-game cause must match the submitted values; a non-event causation token resolves to null, and a cause from another game is rejected.

The kernel event identity is deterministic from game, cycle, game event, container, kernel event type, operation, and status, and submission occurs after the container is upserted.

Cursor persistence validates that the cycle exists in the game and repeats durable event-linkage validation before merging. Existing trace telemetry is preserved, and the merge does not increment cycle revision, alter
, or emit a game-cycle lifecycle event.

An absent optional runtime or an ordinary optional trace submission failure yields no trace result. Required-runtime mode surfaces that failure. Once the kernel event has been emitted, cursor-persistence failure is always an error, including optional mode, because the durable join would otherwise be incomplete. Retry reuses the deterministic kernel event identity, so a failed cursor write can be repaired without a duplicate kernel event.

metadata. Kernel-to-game navigation uses the protected game-event identity, game, correlation, and cause metadata together with

No kernel table or column is added. The join uses protected JSON metadata already stored on kernel trace events and the game cycle's existing trace JSON cursor.
